speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of decreased vision and seeing black spots in the right eye. He reports no pain, and the left eye is asymptomatic. He mentions being treated for fungal esophagitis 6 months ago and was diagnosed with Kaposi's sarcoma 2 years ago.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Decreased vision and black spots in the right eye. I also have No pain, Left eye is asymptomatic. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is an interesting history, but given your AIDS diagnosis, we must consider opportunistic infections like Cytomegalovirus (CMV) retinitis or Toxoplasmosis as well. Can you tell me if you have any recent fever, night sweats, or weight loss? REQUEST TEST: CMV_PCR; REQUEST TEST: Toxoplasma_IgG

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: CMV_PCR: NORMAL READINGS; Toxoplasma_IgG: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Cytomegalovirus Retinitis (pseudotumor or atypical presentation), despite negative PCR, given AIDS history and visual field loss. I recommend immediate fundus photography and visual field testing to confirm retinal involvement.
